Marissa — quick tech responses below, happy to expand into a one-pager and stitch in links to internal runbooks.

RBAC
- Model: Role-based with support for custom roles and scoping via resource tags (project/tenant). Built-in roles: owner/admin, developer, analyst/viewer, support. Custom roles can be created with fine-grained permissions (read/write/invoke/manage).
- Enforcement: Policy engine enforces least-privilege for API keys, token scopes, and console actions. We can create "transaction-reader" style roles for customers.

Support access / Break-glass
- Workflow: Support access is just-in-time (JIT) via an approval flow (customer ticket + internal approver). Break-glass is supported but requires an escalation ticket plus documented justification.
- Session controls: Support sessions use ephemeral creds, are recorded at API-call level, and all actions are logged with user id and originating support ticket. For console-level troubleshooting we capture session metadata and attach to ticket.

Audit logs & retention
- Events captured: API calls (including requester and resource), admin/permission changes, model inference invocation metadata (no persistent user prompt storage outside configured retention), and support session metadata.
- Retention: Default log retention is 13 months; can be configured per-account (options: 3m/6m/13m/36m) or exported to customer SIEM via S3 + notification or via our Splunk/Datadog connectors.

Data residency & PII handling
- Region-locked deployments: We offer US and EU region pinning for customer tenant data. Production instances can be provisioned in a specified region; cross-region replication is opt-in.
- Deletion: We support both logical and hard-delete workflows. Customers can request account data purge via API (hard-delete) or request retention-based purge; deletion SLA depends on dataset size but standard is 30 days for hard-delete completion and confirmation.
- Export: Customer data export APIs available for e-discovery; we log exports and provide signed URLs for transfer.

Encryption & KMS
- At-rest: AES-256 encryption by default.
- Customer-managed keys: Supported via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault integrations; HSM-backed key options for enterprise bundles.
